A **chosen covariant first-variation decomposition** is data consisting of an Euler–Lagrange expression $E_\phi[\eta]$, the $n$-form linear in a field variation $\eta$ left after spacetime derivatives have been moved off $\eta$ by integration by parts, and a covariant $(n-1)$-form $\theta(\phi;\eta)$, also linear in $\eta$, such that
$$\delta\mathcal L=E_\phi[\delta\phi]+d\theta(\phi;\delta\phi)$$
for every admitted smooth finite-dimensional family of fields. The choice of $\theta$ is part of the data and need not be unique. A solution has $E_\phi=0$; a linearized solution $\delta\phi$ at $\phi$ has $\delta E_\phi[\delta\phi]=0$.

Let $n\ge2$, let $M$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth $n$-manifold, and let $g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,\ldots,+)$. Write $\boldsymbol\epsilon_g$ for its oriented metric volume form. Let $\nabla$ be its Levi-Civita connection, the unique torsion-free, metric-compatible connection. Let $\phi=(g,\psi)$ denote a smooth section of a specified field bundle $\pi:E\to M$, including the metric and any other dynamical fields $\psi$ that are smooth tensor fields with the pullback action of spacetime diffeomorphisms. An admitted field family is a smooth map $\Phi:P\times M\to E$ with $\pi(\Phi(p,x))=x$, where $P$ is a finite-dimensional smooth parameter manifold; for $v\in T_pP$, $\delta_v\phi$ is the derivative of $\Phi$ along any smooth parameter curve with initial velocity $v$. A **finite-jet Lagrangian $n$-form** is a smooth spacetime $n$-form $\mathcal L(\phi)$ whose coordinate coefficients depend smoothly on the field components and finitely many spacetime derivatives. It is **diffeomorphism-covariant** when pullback by every admitted local diffeomorphism $\Psi$ satisfies $\mathcal L(\Psi^*\phi)=\Psi^*\mathcal L(\phi)$.

A **chosen covariant first-variation decomposition** is data consisting of an Euler–Lagrange expression $E_\phi[\eta]$, the $n$-form linear in a field variation $\eta$ left after spacetime derivatives have been moved off $\eta$ by integration by parts, and a covariant $(n-1)$-form $\theta(\phi;\eta)$, also linear in $\eta$, such that
$$\delta\mathcal L=E_\phi[\delta\phi]+d\theta(\phi;\delta\phi)$$
for every admitted smooth finite-dimensional family of fields. The choice of $\theta$ is part of the data and need not be unique. A solution has $E_\phi=0$; a linearized solution $\delta\phi$ at $\phi$ has $\delta E_\phi[\delta\phi]=0$.

A **stationary solution with generator $\xi$** is a solution $\phi$ and a fixed smooth spacetime vector field $\xi$ such that $\mathcal L_\xi\phi=0$. Thus $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, so $\xi$ is a Killing field of $g$. A **bifurcate Killing horizon** is a pair of smooth null hypersurfaces generated by this Killing flow: $\xi$ is nonzero, null, tangent and normal on each hypersurface away from their transverse intersection $B$, and $\xi=0$ on $B$. Fix a compact, oriented, boundaryless, spacelike embedded codimension-two submanifold $B\subset M$. Choose a future-directed unit timelike normal $u$ and a chosen unit spacelike normal $n_B$ along $B$, orthogonal to each other, and define the binormal $\epsilon_{ab}=2u_{[a}(n_B)_{b]}$, so $\epsilon_{ab}\epsilon^{ab}=-2$. Orient $B$ compatibly with the spacetime orientation and this normal frame so that, on $B$, $(\boldsymbol\epsilon_g)_{ab a_3\ldots a_n}=\epsilon_{ab}(dA_B)_{a_3\ldots a_n}$; here $dA_B$ is the positive volume form of the induced metric with that orientation. The horizon is **nondegenerate** when the fixed normalization of $\xi$ gives a constant $\kappa>0$ on $B$ with $\nabla_a\xi_b=\kappa\epsilon_{ab}$ there; $\kappa$ is its surface gravity. Variations keep $\xi$ and the embedded surface $B$ fixed.

For such data define the **Noether current** $(n-1)$-form
$$J_\xi:=\theta(\phi;\mathcal L_\xi\phi)-\iota_\xi\mathcal L.$$
Choose a smooth covariant $(n-2)$-form $Q_\xi$ on a neighborhood of the admitted field data and define the residual constraint form $C_\xi:=J_\xi-dQ_\xi$. Require $C_\xi=0$ on the selected solution and, for each admitted linearized perturbation used below, require its fixed-$\xi$ variation $\delta C_\xi=0$. These are explicit on-shell and linearized-constraint conditions; no existence or global exactness of $Q_\xi$ follows merely from closure of a presymplectic current. The pullback of $Q_\xi$ is required to be globally compatible on the integration region.

Boundary data consist of a smooth solution space with specified falloff, a family of closed codimension-two surfaces $S_R$ approaching the asymptotic boundary, and finite oriented smooth singular hypersurface chains $C_R$ with $\partial C_R=S_R-B$. Normalize $\xi$ and the boundary units so that $H_\xi$ has the corresponding Hamiltonian units. With a fixed boundary-term convention, define the charge-variation one-form by
$$\alpha_\xi(\delta\phi):=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R}\bigl(\delta Q_\xi-\iota_\xi\theta(\phi;\delta\phi)\bigr).$$
Require this limit to exist and be globally integrable: there is a smooth Hamiltonian charge $H_\xi$ on the specified solution space with $d_{\mathcal S}H_\xi=\alpha_\xi$, where $d_{\mathcal S}$ is the exterior derivative on that solution space. This exactness, and the chosen boundary formula itself, are hypotheses. Other boundary actions or falloff conditions can add terms and require a separately stated charge formula.

If $X$ has local flow $\Phi_t$ and $T$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(r,s)$, its Lie derivative is $$\mathcal L_XT=\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*T,$$ on every local flow domain where this derivative is defined. Here the pullback by the local diffeomorphism $\Phi_t$ acts by $d\Phi_{-t}$ on each contravariant slot and by $d\Phi_t$ on each covariant slot.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$.  For $\omega\in\Omega^k(M)$,
$\mathcal L_X\omega$ is the Lie derivative of $\omega$ regarded as an
alternating covariant tensor.
For every vector field $X$ and differential form $\omega$, $$\mathcal L_X\omega=d(\iota_X\omega)+\iota_X(d\omega).$$

derivations.claim: Differentiate the coordinate curvature identity to obtain delta R^a_bcd=2 nabla_[c delta Gamma^a_d]b and derive delta Gamma from the varied torsion-free metric-compatible conditions. Substitute into P delta R and integrate by parts: the unique derivative-of-delta-g term is 2 E_R^{bcd} nabla_d delta g_bc. Repeated finite integration by parts on matter jets leaves a covariant potential linear in variations of covariant tensor jets.

Apply covariance and the first-variation identity to delta phi=Lie_zeta phi. Cartan and dL=0 give dJ_zeta=-E_phi[Lie_zeta phi], so J is closed on shell. Formula F1 shows every tensor-jet variation contributes only zeta and nabla zeta; the displayed curvature term contributes 2 E_R^{bcd} nabla_d(nabla_b zeta_c+nabla_c zeta_b). Antisymmetry in c,d makes the second summand one half of a commutator, hence curvature times zeta. The only second-derivative term is therefore 2 E_R^{bcd} nabla_d nabla_b zeta_c.

Use the product rule on the unique second-derivative term. Expanding d(X^{cd} nabla_[c zeta_d]) in components with X=-P contracted against the volume form, then antisymmetrizing the two curvature pairs and the form slots, gives the same second-derivative coefficient and sign. The remaining current terms have at most first derivatives of zeta; the canonical recursive integration by parts moves each such derivative onto its coefficient and leaves only a term linear in zeta. The stated standard changes add i_zeta mu, Y(phi;Lie_zeta phi), or dZ.

boundaries.reason: A smooth spacetime and finite tensor data are supplied; no empty spacetime case is asserted.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement and step 3.1 give X=0 when P=0; lower-order W zeta terms remain allowed.
The allowed n=2 case has a zero-dimensional bifurcation surface; the statement explicitly omits dZ in that dimension, and the local derivative-of-generator coefficient remains defined.

The decomposition is pointwise/local and makes no finite-chain endpoint claim.

The result is a decomposition implication, not a biconditional.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, possibly with boundary. For $k\ge1$, $c\in C_k^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ and $\omega\in\Omega^{k-1}(M)$, define integration over a chain by the finite linear sum of its simplex integrals. Then
$$\int_c d\omega=\int_{\partial c}\omega.$$
The zero chain has integral zero. In degree zero the boundary is zero; no degree-minus-one form is required by this statement.

Use the metric, tensor fields, covariant first-variation decomposition, and
Noether current of [[def-tgrx-noether-horizon-data]]. Suppose the Lagrangian is
$$\mathcal L=\ell(g_{ab},R_{abcd},\psi,\nabla\psi,\ldots,\nabla_{(a_1}\cdots\nabla_{a_m)}\psi)\,\boldsymbol\epsilon_g,$$
where $m<\infty$, all fields and coefficients are smooth, and the curvature
argument is algebraic (there are no covariant derivatives of $R_{abcd}$).
Define the Riemann-symmetric derivative $P^{abcd}$ by
$$\delta\ell\big|_{g,\psi,\nabla\psi,\ldots}=P^{abcd}\delta R_{abcd},$$
with $P^{abcd}=-P^{bacd}=-P^{abdc}=P^{cdab}$ and $P^{a[bcd]}=0$.

Use the covariant first-variation potential produced by the finite covariant
integration-by-parts construction on the field jets, up to the stated
potential ambiguities. For each smooth vector field $\zeta$, use the local
Noether potential obtained by covariantly integrating the derivatives of
$\zeta$ in $J_\zeta=\theta(\phi;\mathcal L_\zeta\phi)-\iota_\zeta\mathcal L$
by parts.
Call this the **canonical local representative**: it is defined on a
neighborhood of the fields and generators, is a local covariant primitive of
$J_\zeta$ on shell, and has no independent closed-form addition. The permitted
representative changes are exactly those induced by
$$\mathcal L\mapsto\mathcal L+d\mu,\qquad \theta\mapsto\theta+\delta\mu+d\mathbf Y,$$
and by an exact charge change; here $\mu$ is a covariant $(n-1)$-form and
$\mathbf Y(\phi;\eta)$ is a covariant $(n-2)$-form linear in $\eta$.
Assume the chosen representative is globally compatible on the integration
region. Then it has the form
$$Q_\zeta=W^c\zeta_c+X^{cd}\nabla_{[c}\zeta_{d]} +\mathbf Y(\phi;\mathcal L_\zeta\phi)+dZ,$$
where $W^c$ and $X^{cd}$ are local covariant form-valued coefficients,
$Z$ is a local covariant $(n-3)$-form (the exact term is absent when $n=2$),
and
$$(X^{cd})_{a_3\ldots a_n} =-P^{abcd}(\boldsymbol\epsilon_g)_{ab a_3\ldots a_n}.$$
For the canonical representative before the permitted changes one may take
$\mathbf Y=0$ and $Z=0$.

derivations.claim: Apply the charge decomposition. On B, xi=0 and Lie_xi phi=0, so W xi and the unvaried Y term vanish. The only possible Y variation is Y(phi;Lie_xi delta phi), which covariance identifies with Lie_xi Y(phi;delta phi); Cartan expresses it as i_xi dY+d(i_xiY), whose pullback has zero integral. Stokes removes d(delta Z); i_xi mu and exact charge shifts vanish after pullback/integration. Thus delta integral_B Q=delta integral_B X^{cd} nabla_[c xi_d].

Set w_cd=nabla_[c xi_d]-kappa epsilon_cd. Fixed xi and xi=0 on B imply delta(nabla_c xi^a)=delta Gamma^a_ce xi^e=0, hence delta w_cd=-kappa g_a[d delta epsilon_c]^a. The tangent-tangent binormal variation vanishes because the binormal annihilates tangent vectors, and normalization removes the normal-normal antisymmetric component; delta w is normal-tangent. Stationarity gives Lie_xi X=0; at B this is invariance under the normal Lorentz boost. Boost weight zero implies invariance under reflection of both normals, while a normal-tangent component changes sign, so its pullback contraction with X vanishes.

On B, nabla_a xi_b=kappa epsilon_ab and X^{cd}epsilon_cd=-P^{abcd}epsilon_ab epsilon_cd dA_B by F4 and the orientation convention. Vary X^{cd}(kappa epsilon_cd+w_cd): w=0 in the background, its variation term integrates to zero by step 1.2, and kappa is fixed. Therefore delta integral_B Q=kappa delta integral_B X epsilon=-(kappa)delta integral_B P epsilon epsilon dA=(hbar kappa/(2 pi k_B))delta S_W.

derivations.claim: Vary J at fixed xi. Linearity of theta in its variation slot and Lie_xi phi=0 remove coefficient-variation terms; fixed xi gives delta(Lie_xi phi)=Lie_xi delta phi. Covariance changes theta(phi;Lie_xi delta phi) into Lie_xi theta(phi;delta phi). E_phi=0 and Cartan then yield delta J=d(i_xi theta).
Differentiate C_xi=J_xi-dQ_xi with delta C_xi=0. Since spacetime d is fixed, delta J=d(delta Q). Combining with step 1.1 gives d(delta Q-i_xi theta)=0.

Apply Stokes to the finite oriented chain C_R. Its boundary S_R-B gives equal integrals of the closed form on S_R and B. The B pullback of i_xi theta is zero because xi=0 there. The specified boundary limit is delta H by A1, hence delta H=integral_B delta Q.
The charge representative is the class in F3, so L1 applies to the horizon integral from step 3.1 and gives delta H=(hbar kappa/(2 pi k_B))delta S_W at fixed background kappa.

For ell=R/(16 pi G), differentiate the scalar curvature contraction on algebraic curvature tensors to obtain P=(g^{ac}g^{bd}-g^{ad}g^{bc})/(32 pi G). Contracting the normalized binormal gives -1/(8 pi G); substituting in the entropy functional yields S_W=k_B A_B/(4G hbar).
